senses.definition: (anatomy) A biological organ of vertebrates that controls breathing and oxygenates the blood.

quotes.text: I made a speaking trumpet of my hands and commenced to whoop “Ahoy!” and “Hello!” at the top of my lungs. […] The Colonel woke up, and, after asking what in brimstone was the matter, opened his mouth and roared “Hi!” and “Hello!” like the bull of Bashan.
quotes.reference: 1913, Joseph C[rosby] Lincoln, chapter VII, in Mr. Pratt’s Patients, New York, N.Y.; London: D[aniel] Appleton and Company, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (in the plural) Capacity for exercise or exertion; breath.
examples: He no longer has the lungs to play long rallies like he used to.

senses.definition: That which supplies oxygen or fresh air, such as trees, parklands, forest, etc., to a place.

quotes.text: Afterwards he found that the vague feeling of alarm had spread to the clients of the underground railway, and that the Sunday excursionists began to return from all the South-Western "lungs" - Barnes, Wimbledon, Richmond Park, Kew, and so forth - at unnaturally early hours[.]
quotes.reference: 1898, H.G. Wells, The War of the Worlds, London: William Heinemann, page 123:
